source: Yu & LaValle, ICRA 2010, Sec. IV Fig. 4 and Tables III-IV (worked numbers in T-RO 2012 Table III / Fig. 12-13)
notes: Event order read from ICRA10 Fig. 4 (bold observations only): y_x on s1, split s2->s3,s4, y_e on s3, merge s1+s3->s5, s5 disappears revealing 1 or 2 agents with probability 0.5 each (the disappear update multiplies by P(s5=x) and renormalises). 'no null event, true positive rate 0.9' is encoded as obs_model. ICRA10 Table IV / T-RO Algorithm 2: when x_i=0 an exit is impossible and the enter/null pieces of THAT ENTRY are rescaled to sum to the entry's mass p_j (no mass leaves the entry). This reproduces every row of T-RO Table III. Dropping the impossible mass and renormalising globally gives alternative_global_renormalization_final (0.0833/0.1667/0.75) instead, which does NOT match the paper. The 'slightly more complicated' variant (bold+lightened observations, 5 agents per shadow, '135 entries') is reproduced when both y_e observations on s4 precede the merge: see tor_fig12_complex.json and docs/notes/probabilistic_extraction.md section 6.
monte_carlo_semantics: A rejection-sampling Monte Carlo that samples e ~ P(e|y) and DISCARDS a trial when it samples an exit from an empty shadow converges to alternative_global_renormalization_final (400k trials: 0.0838/0.1671/0.7491). A Monte Carlo that instead resamples among enter/null in that case converges to expected_final_marginal (400k trials: 0.0774/0.1543/0.7684). The paper's 1000-trial numbers (0.079/0.154/0.767) are within 2 standard errors of both, so a Monte Carlo baseline used to test the exact filter must use the second (per-entry) rule.
